• Competition Act passed in 2002.
• Based on Raghavan Committee.
• Replaced MRTP.
• Appeals go to NCLAT.
• Quasi-judicial authority.

items: Remember that the Competition Act 2002 replaced MRTP based on the Raghavan Committee recommendations.
Appeals regarding the Competition Act are submitted to NCLAT, not directly to the High Court.
Identify the nature of the authority: it is a quasi-judicial authority.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Competition Act was officially passed in 2002.
Its enactment was based on recommendations by the Raghavan Committee.
The law replaced the earlier Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) framework.
The governing body operates as a quasi-judicial authority.
Appeals against decisions go directly to NCLAT.
